insight: When materializing decomposed epics in beads on a repo whose directory contains a dot (e.g. ryanhenderson.dev), bd init writes .beads/metadata.json with dolt_database equal to the directory name; embedded Dolt rejects dots and bd commands fail with 'invalid database name'. Fix: edit .beads/metadata.json dolt_database to the underscore-form (ryanhenderson_dev) which matches the existing .beads/embeddeddolt subdirectory bd already created.

For solo-dev personal sites, the architect's decomposition should fold cross-cutting concerns (single-source helpers, build-time smoke tests, scoped tokens, CSP hashes, lazy-load assertions, frozen lockfile) into per-epic acceptance criteria rather than spawning separate cross-cutting epics. Separate 'testing' / 'devops' / 'security' epics fragment ownership and create coordination cost out of proportion to a single-author project. The architect skill's 'Cross-cutting concerns folded into per-epic ACs' table is the right pattern; aim for ~15-20 such concerns mapped to specific epic ACs.

When the advisor fleet flags YAGNI items (e.g. Atom-alongside-RSS, scripted DNS, Satori OG) but the user has explicitly chosen them, do NOT silently drop them in decomposition. Honor the user's choice, embed the advisor's mitigations as non-negotiable per-epic ACs (e.g. scoped CF token, static fallback PNG, RSS draft-leak smoke test), and surface the kept-vs-dropped negotiation explicitly at Gate 2 so the trade-off is auditable.

When testing Astro 5 content collection schemas (zod), extract the schema definitions into a pure module (e.g. src/content/schemas.ts) and have src/content/config.ts import them and wire them into defineCollection. Then test the schemas directly with vitest -- they no longer require booting the astro:content / astro/loaders virtual modules. The schema's .strict() rejection, default values, and required-field enforcement become unit-testable in isolation. Without this split, vitest can't import config.ts because astro:content only resolves during astro dev/build.

Grep-style enforcement scripts (e.g. forbidding direct getCollection() calls outside a single helper module) MUST scan whole-file with multi-line regex (text.matchAll on the raw string) and compute line numbers from match index, NOT split on 
 and run a per-line regex. A per-line scan misses multi-line calls like getCollection(
  "blog"
) and aliased imports like { getCollection as gc } from "astro:content". Pin the enforcement with integration tests that exercise: (a) the happy path, (b) a single-line offender, (c) a multi-line call, (d) an aliased import, and (e) an unrelated function with the same name (false-positive guard). Without the integration tests, a regression in the regex silently disables the gate.

Astro 5's content layer glob loader derives entry id from the relative path within base, NOT from the basename. So src/content/blog/foo.mdx and src/content/blog/sub/foo.mdx coexist with distinct ids ('foo' and 'sub/foo') and Astro itself does NOT detect the slug collision. If the spec requires within-collection slug uniqueness (slug = filename minus .mdx), you need a separate pre-build gate (e.g. scripts/check-content-slugs.mjs) that walks each collection directory and flags duplicate basenames across paths. This is independent of Astro's own validation and is the only way to catch the 'two files render at the same URL' failure mode before the build.

For Astro projects, 'pnpm lint' should run 'astro check' (not bare tsc). astro check feeds .astro templates and the generated .astro/types.d.ts (CollectionEntry types) through TypeScript so type errors in component frontmatter and content collection consumers surface together. Bare tsc misses .astro files entirely. When set up: install @astrojs/check, add 'lint': 'astro check' to package.json, and gate CI on it.

Design tokens that need to drive both CSS variables AND build-time renderers (Satori for OG images, Shiki for syntax highlighting) must live in a single TypeScript module — Satori cannot resolve CSS custom properties, so concrete hex/numeric values are mandatory. Generate tokens.css from tokens.ts via a small Node script wired into pnpm build (Node 22.6+ runs .ts via type-stripping; .mjs scripts can dynamic-import .ts). Enforce zero drift with a vitest test that compares tokensToCss() output to the committed CSS file. Reserve consumer-side variable names (e.g. --shiki-fg) inside the token module so downstream epics cannot drift them.

Astro CSS scoping injects 'data-astro-cid-*' attributes between authored attributes; tests asserting attribute order with simple regex break. Use [^>]* between attrs or parse the tag, not literal-order regex.
On routes with noindex (e.g. 404), do NOT emit <link rel=canonical>. A canonical on a noindex page tells crawlers to treat that URL as the canonical destination — semantically backwards.

Skip-link CLS trap: switching from position:absolute(off-screen) to position:static on :focus reflows the page when keyboard users tab in. Use translateY(-200%) → translateY(0) so the link stays absolutely positioned in both states. Required to keep CLS=0.

When multiple Vitest files all assert against `dist/` produced by `pnpm build`, putting `execSync('pnpm build')` in each file's `beforeAll` causes parallel build invocations to race on the same output paths and produce intermittent failures. Solution: consolidate the build into Vitest's `globalSetup` (run once before any suite) and have each test file just verify the artifacts it expects already exist. See vitest.config.ts `globalSetup: ['./tests/setup/build.ts']` pattern in this repo.

Astro emits HTML attributes in source-declaration order, not a guaranteed order. Tests that chain multiple attributes in a single regex (e.g. /class="x"[^>]*href="y"[^>]*target=/) are brittle: they break when authors reorder the source attributes or after Astro upgrades. Capture the tag with /<a\b[^>]*>/g, filter by a stable selector (a class or data-* hook), then assert each attribute with a separate .toMatch on the captured tag.

Astro getStaticPaths runs in an isolated module context — module-scope helpers (functions/consts) declared in the same .astro file are NOT in scope. Inline the logic or export+import from another module. Symptom: 'X is not defined' at build time despite local declaration.

Hand-rolled XML feeds (e.g. Atom) MUST escape ALL attribute values, not just element text. URL strings interpolated into href= or id= produce invalid XML if the URL contains & < > or quotes. Use escapeXml() on every attribute value, even ones that 'look safe'.

Astro check:content-source-style regexes that grep for forbidden patterns (e.g. getCollection("blog")) can match comments and JSDoc text. Rephrase comments to avoid the literal pattern (use 'the raw collection loader' instead of the literal call). Don't weaken the regex.

Satori 0.26 treats children: [] as multi-child and demands explicit display: flex/contents/none on the parent — even though the array is empty. Fix: when building a Satori element tree with a helper, omit the children key entirely for leaf nodes (length 0) instead of passing an empty array. Otherwise hairline divider divs (width/height/backgroundColor only, no children) trigger 'Expected <div> to have explicit display'.

For SEO migration cutover commits (Jekyll → Astro): the retirement commit must atomically include BOTH the deletion of legacy source files AND the public/_redirects file. Splitting them creates a window where audited legacy URLs return 404 (STPA B3 timing issue). Pin this with a test that parses both docs/migration/legacy-urls.txt and public/_redirects and asserts every audited REDIRECT row has a matching rule, and every rule traces back to an audit row — drift in either direction breaks SEO link equity.

CSP for Astro static sites: enumerate all inline <script> bodies in dist/ across every HTML route, sha256-hash each one, and emit them as 'sha256-...' sources in script-src on the /* block. Style-src can stay 'unsafe-inline' (per-component scoped <style> blocks are too volatile to hash; not a meaningful XSS vector for a static site). Wire a check script that walks dist/ and asserts the union of observed inline-script hashes equals the set declared in public/_headers — fail the build on either missing (would be blocked at runtime) or stale (silently grew permission). Provide a --fix flag that rewrites _headers but never wire it into CI.

When testing a Node script via spawn from inside Vitest, use async spawn rather than spawnSync. spawnSync blocks the event loop, so any in-process mock HTTP server the child needs to call will hang because the parent thread cannot accept connections. Caught by IV-5 provision-cf idempotency test — initial spawnSync version timed out at 30s on every run.

CSP script-src must include 'wasm-unsafe-eval' (CSP3) for any feature that compiles WebAssembly at runtime — Pagefind, comlink, sql.js, etc. 'self' alone is insufficient: WASM compilation is gated by the same directive as eval. wasm-unsafe-eval is narrower than 'unsafe-eval' (no eval()/new Function()), so the threat model around build-time-fingerprinted WASM is unchanged. Caught by IV Playwright suite trying to drive Pagefind under prod CSP.

When using lychee-action@v2 against a static dist/, use '--root-dir $(pwd)/dist' (absolute path required) — NOT '--base dist'. Lychee 0.24+ rejects relative paths for --base. The --root-dir flag resolves root-relative hrefs like /posts/foo/ against the dist directory. In GH Actions: --root-dir ${{ github.workspace }}/dist.

Astro static sites with no client islands have 0-byte resource-summary:script:size in Lighthouse — inline scripts (e.g., ThemeBoot) roll up into the document size. When setting LHCI bundle budgets for such sites, expect script:size=0 baseline; cap can be generous (25 KB+) since real client JS only appears when components opt in. Tighten only if you want a hard 'no JS' posture.

For Astro/static-site CodeQL workflows, omit the github/codeql-action/autobuild step. CodeQL traces JS/TS sources without a tsc-style build, and Astro's build is not a conventional compile. Document the omission inline so future maintainers don't add it back. Keep init+analyze@v3 with category '/language:javascript-typescript' and queries 'security-extended'.

@vitest/coverage-v8 has a strict runtime peer-version match with vitest. When adding it, align the lower bound in package.json (e.g., bump 'vitest' lower bound to match the coverage package version). Otherwise 'pnpm update' could resolve a future mismatch where the peer check fails at test time. The lockfile protects the current install but not future updates.

Avoid scheduling GitHub Actions cron at top-of-hour ('0 H * * *') — that's the high-load slot and queue times balloon. Pick an off-peak minute (e.g., '23 6 * * 1') for predictable start. Also: actions/upload-artifact and download-artifact are versioned independently since v4; v7 upload + v8 download is wire-compatible (both Artifact Service v2) but a mismatch is worth aligning during the next Dependabot bump.

CodeQL on private GitHub repos requires GitHub Advanced Security (paid). On public repos it's free. If a custom codeql.yml workflow fails with 'Code scanning is not enabled for this repository', check repo visibility first — making a personal repo public is usually the right fix; paying for GHAS on a personal site is overkill.

When CodeQL is enabled on a repo for the first time AND a large PR is open, the GitHub Advanced Security app posts a 'CodeQL' PR status check that fails when the PR introduces high-severity alerts vs base. This check is independent of any CodeQL workflow's own pass/fail. To make the PR mergeable, either (a) fix real findings or (b) triage and dismiss false positives via the alerts API: PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts/{n} with state=dismissed + dismissed_reason in {'false positive','won't fix','used in tests'} + a dismissed_comment explaining the rationale. Common false positives in test/build code: js/path-injection where there's an explicit prefix-match guard CodeQL doesn't recognize; js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor on .not.toMatch() where unanchored is intentional; js/bad-tag-filter on regex parsers of own-emitted controlled HTML.

Cloudflare Pages does NOT auto-deploy on push to master unless either (a) the CF Pages GitHub App is installed AND a Pages project for the repo exists watching the production branch, or (b) a workflow step explicitly runs 'wrangler pages deploy'. If 'gh api repos/<o>/<r>/deployments' shows no entries with environment='Production' despite many pushes, no auto-deploy is wired up. Quick diagnosis: 'npx wrangler pages project list' from an authenticated wrangler — if the project doesn't exist, that's why production is 404'ing or stale.

cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3 defaults to installing wrangler 3.x (3.90.0 at time of writing) which has auth issues on 'pages deploy' against modern API tokens (returns HTTP 400 / code 9106). Always pin 'wranglerVersion: "4"' in the action's 'with:' block. The same API token that fails with wrangler 3 works with wrangler 4.

cloudflare/wrangler-action auto-detects the package manager from the project's lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock / package-lock.json) and installs wrangler with it. If your deploy job doesn't run the matching setup action (pnpm/action-setup, yarn, etc.), the wrangler install fails with 'Unable to locate executable file: pnpm'. Fix: pass 'packageManager: npm' to the action so it uses npm regardless of lockfile. The deploy job doesn't need pnpm for anything else — it just downloads the dist artifact and shells out to wrangler.

GitHub Actions secret values pasted via the web UI textarea can pick up a trailing newline or leading whitespace, causing CF API 9106 ('Authentication failed') even with a known-good token. If a token verifies via 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<id>/pages/projects/<name>' locally but CI gets 9106, the secret value almost certainly has paste artifact. Re-paste cleanly (cmd+v with no manual edits, no trailing whitespace) and the failed deploy job re-run will succeed.

GitHub repo Branch Protection Rulesets (the newer rule-based system, not the older branch-protection-rules API) enforce 'allowed_merge_methods' per-rule. If the rule has 'allowed_merge_methods: ["squash"]', 'gh pr merge --merge' fails with 'Merge commits are not allowed on this repository' even if the repo's general settings (allow_merge_commit/allow_squash_merge/allow_rebase_merge) are all true. Check 'gh api repos/<o>/<r>/rulesets' to see what's actually enforced; use 'gh pr merge --squash' if that's the only allowed method.

GitHub Actions sometimes silently fails to fire the 'pull_request' event when a PR is opened — observed when the branch was created and pushed in close temporal proximity to other CI activity, or when the PR has merge conflicts at open time. Workarounds: (a) push an empty commit to re-trigger via the synchronize event, (b) use 'gh workflow run --ref <branch>' to manually dispatch (requires workflow_dispatch trigger). After a force-push following rebase, pull_request typically does fire normally.

Astro static-site routing: any file or directory in src/pages/ whose leaf name starts with '_' is excluded from the build (per node_modules/astro/dist/core/routing/manifest/create.js — 'if (name[0] === "_") continue;'). Use this to 'soft hide' routes (e.g. src/pages/_blog/posts/[slug].astro, src/pages/work/_[slug].astro) without deleting source — files stay in tree for easy restore via rename. Underscore prefix works on both filenames AND directory names.

For domains delegated to Cloudflare nameservers, DNS changes happen in the Cloudflare dashboard, NOT at the registrar (eNom, GoDaddy, etc.). Verify delegation: 'dig +short NS <domain>' should show the Cloudflare nameservers (e.g. dale.ns.cloudflare.com). The registrar only holds the registration; nameserver delegation happens once at zone setup, after which all A/AAAA/CNAME edits live in CF. Common confusion when changing apex DNS to point at a new origin (e.g. CF Pages project).
